best: Every sheet is split into titled functional blocks with left-to-right power paths (pack path, four-switch stage with sense filters, bucks with dividers) drawn as wires, set-point annotations and numbered design notes, so most checks against the datasheets need no net searching.
worst: Stacked ground/thermal-pad pin numbers pile into unreadable smears under the TPD6S300 and TPS25751, and a few texts collide (J113 'LOAD PACK_P' on the block border and PACK_P label, CHG_INH label over the J302 pin name, tight pin numbers next to MCU labels)

The power FETs are box symbols (SiZ240DT halves, BSC007N04LS6 with G/D/S boxes) so the four-switch bridge and back-to-back protection FETs do not read as the textbook transistor drawings, and gate drive/bootstrap/sense nets between the bridge and the BQ25756 are joined only by labels
Uneven use of space: the MCU and 3V3 sheets and the lower part of the Cells sheet leave large empty areas, the NTC wire block is four label-only connectors, and TP412 floats alone outside any block
